solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Catholic dresser for the most part is more assured

indicators.note: most but not all of the word is used, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for Catholic
an almery (ambry) is a cupboard or dresser

explanation.surface: A Catholic who mostly gets dressed properly feels more confident.
explanation.walkthrough: An almery, also spelt ambry, is an old word for a cupboard, often one in a church for sacred vessels.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone calmer is more composed and self-possessed, so 'is more assured' describes them.

clue.text: Tropical background in which jolly Jacks climb?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a backdrop in the figurative sense, as when a period is the setting for events; 'tropical' here means using a trope, not hot
second meaning: the sails of a ship, up whose rigging sailors (jolly jack tars) go aloft

explanation.surface: A painted tropical scene where cheerful sailors scramble up the masts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tropical' tempts you towards palm trees, but it means figurative. A jack tar is a sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: Canvas is what a painter works on and so a metaphorical setting; it is also the sailcloth of a ship.

clue.text: Local's narrow lane is left clipped all right

indicators.note: something clipped has had its end cut off, so the last letter goes

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for left
okeh is a variant spelling of OK

explanation.surface: A villager says their narrow lane is fine, apart from being cut back on the left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Local's' signals a dialect word, here from East Anglia.
explanation.definitionFit: Loke is a dialect word, chiefly Norfolk, for a lane or narrow passage, hence 'Local's'.

clue.text: Biden's confusion on leaving sweet dish

indicators.note: the short form of 'on' departs from the dish, so it is taken out

parts.note: a mousse is a light whipped dessert
o' is a shortened form of 'on', as in 'o' nights'

explanation.surface: The US President is muddled about having walked away from a pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: MOUSSE without O leaves MUSSE. Biden stands for American usage: muss or musse is chiefly North American for a mess.
explanation.definitionFit: Musse, a variant of muss, is an American word for disorder or a state of mess.

clue.text: Predator's back amidst drunken revelry

indicators.note: the run of letters is read backwards, from right to left
the letters sit amid the following words, spanning their junction

parts.note: the letters straddling the two words

explanation.surface: A predator is back among the drunken partygoers.
explanation.walkthrough: drunkEN REvelry hides ENRE, which backwards is ERNE.
explanation.definitionFit: An erne is a sea eagle, a bird of prey.

clue.text: Covers put in place again somehow increase runs

indicators.note: 'somehow' says the letters come together in some unstated way, so they are rearranged

parts.note: the twelve letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A cricket side has its cover fielders replaced, which somehow lifts the scoring.
explanation.definitionFit: Reinsurance is insurance cover renewed or laid off again, so reinsurances are covers arranged a second time.

clue.text: Stitch up's certainly trapping you in Perpignan

indicators.note: one word catches and holds another inside it

parts.note: sure means certainly
tu is French for you; Perpignan is a French city

explanation.surface: Being framed for something definitely catches you out in a French town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stitch up' looks like the slang for framing someone, but here it means to sew. Perpignan signals French.
explanation.definitionFit: To suture is to sew up a wound surgically.

clue.text: Take a starter that's been minced — this

definitions.text: Take a starter that's been minced — this

indicators.note: minced food is chopped finely, so the letters are cut up and put back in new order

parts.note: the twelve letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A waiter offers a first course of minced meat and names it.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: the dish really is a starter made of minced raw meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Steak tartare is raw minced beef, often served as a starter, so the whole clue describes it.

clue.text: Sadly it's up to a believer in a brave new world?

definitions.text: a believer in a brave new world?

indicators.note: 'sadly' implies things have gone badly wrong, so the letters are in disarray

parts.note: the eight letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: It is sadly up to an idealist to imagine a better world.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that Huxley's Brave New World is a dystopia, though the phrase suggests an ideal society.
explanation.definitionFit: A Utopiast is an idealist who believes in a perfect society, Utopia.

clue.text: Lake held by peacekeepers — area to freshen up bones

indicators.note: the peacekeepers grip the lake, so it sits inside them

parts.note: the United Nations sends peacekeeping forces
L is the abbreviation for lake
A is the abbreviation for area

indicators.note: in a down clue 'up' means the word is written bottom to top, that is backwards

parts.note: to air a room is to freshen it

explanation.surface: UN troops at a lake air a region where bones lie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Freshen' reads as part of the surface, but it supplies the word that is turned upwards at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Ulnaria is the plural of ulnare, a wrist bone on the ulna side.

clue.text: Protest about new nuisance — like those on HS2 say

parts.note: to rail is to complain bitterly

indicators.note: 'about' means around, so one word wraps around the letter

parts.note: a bore is a tiresome person or thing
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: Objectors complain about the new high-speed railway being a nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: HS2 is a British high-speed rail line that has drawn many protests, which makes the surface topical.
explanation.definitionFit: Railborne means carried by rail, as the passengers on a train line are, HS2 being an example.

clue.text: Last in line? Sort to stop atop (6, two words)

indicators.note: in a down entry, sitting atop means being written above, so that part comes first

parts.note: to end something is to stop it
to man is to handle or manage, so sort out

explanation.surface: The person at the back of the queue sets about stopping things at the top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'atop' places END above MAN in this down entry. An end man sat at either end of the line in a minstrel show.
explanation.definitionFit: An end man is the performer at the end of a line of minstrels, so literally the last one.

clue.text: A Brief Encounter? Route's redone with hot mate about

indicators.note: something redone is made over in a new form, so its letters are rearranged
'about' here means turned around and shuffled together

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A trip is reorganised so that one can go off with an attractive partner.
explanation.walkthrough: Brief Encounter is the 1945 film of a short, unconsummated love affair; 'hot' adds colour to the mate.
explanation.definitionFit: An amourette is a petty or passing love affair, a brief romantic encounter.

clue.text: Jack in Jozi spinning German's one film

indicators.note: spinning turns the whole thing round, so it is read the other way

parts.note: ein is German for one
a skin is a thin film or layer

explanation.surface: A man in Johannesburg is twirling a German's single movie.
explanation.walkthrough: EIN plus SKIN, reversed. Jozi is a nickname for Johannesburg, and 'jack' means nothing at all, as in 'you know jack'.
explanation.definitionFit: Niksnie is South African slang for nothing, the same as 'jack' in 'jack all'.

clue.text: Loyal wife of legend, one enthralled by purpose

indicators.note: to be enthralled is to be held captive, so one part is held inside the other

parts.note: an end is an aim or purpose
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A devoted wife in an old tale is captivated by a single aim.
explanation.walkthrough: I goes inside END.
explanation.definitionFit: Enid is the faithful wife of Geraint in Arthurian legend, celebrated by Tennyson for her loyalty.

clue.text: Classicist's very well indeed with work to sharpen reading aid

parts.note: surface padding, hinting that op is short for Latin opus
op is short for opus, Latin for work
top, as in tip-top, means excellent
to hone a blade is to sharpen it

explanation.surface: A Latin scholar is doing nicely with a job sharpening a device for reading.
explanation.walkthrough: This parse is uncertain: 'Classicist's' seems to point to op as Latin opus, and 'with' lets work come first.
explanation.definitionFit: An optophone is a device that turns printed letters into sounds so blind people can read.

clue.text: Is cracking prize, figuratively, a song?

indicators.note: to crack something is to break into it, so one part goes inside the other

parts.note: the palm is a figurative prize, as in 'bear the palm'
the contraction 's stands for is

explanation.surface: Is a terrific award, so to speak, a sort of song?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cracking' reads as 'excellent', but it means breaking in: S enters PALM.
explanation.definitionFit: A psalm is a sacred song or hymn, especially one from the Book of Psalms.

clue.text: A crowd starts to know instinctively what goes on after play?

parts.note: taken as written
a press is a crowd or throng

indicators.note: the starts of the following words, their opening letters, are taken

parts.note: the opening letters of the two words

explanation.surface: A crowd begins to sense by instinct what will follow the game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Play' sounds like a match or show, but it means a day of skiing.
explanation.definitionFit: Après-ski is the socialising that follows a day on the slopes.

clue.text: Blow away tips of unfading flowers found hidden in grass

indicators.note: the letters are tucked inside another word, so that word contains them

parts.note: a snout is slang for a police informer, as is a grass

indicators.note: the tips of words are their first letters

parts.note: the first letters of the three words

explanation.surface: Wind scatters the heads of everlasting blooms tucked away in a lawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grass' looks like a lawn, but it is the British slang for an informer.
explanation.definitionFit: To snuff out a candle is to blow it out, to extinguish it.

clue.text: Exploitative profit-maker beside a horse-drawn carriage

indicators.note: one part is placed next to the other, so the two simply join up

parts.note: arb is short for arbitrageur, who profits from price differences
taken as written

explanation.surface: A greedy trader rides alongside an old coach.
explanation.definitionFit: An arba (araba) is a heavy horse-drawn wagon used in Turkey and the Middle East.

clue.text: Explosively out, instanter — such is sneezing

indicators.note: an explosion scatters things, so the letters are blown apart and rearranged

parts.note: the twelve letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Something bursts out immediately, which is just what a sneeze does.
explanation.walkthrough: Instanter is a legal word meaning at once. The surface is apt: a sneeze comes out explosively and instantly.
explanation.definitionFit: Sternutation is the formal or medical term for the act of sneezing.

clue.text: Being outside stop wasting time round rings with light

indicators.note: the being goes on the outside, wrapping around the rest

parts.note: ens is the philosophers' word for being or existence

indicators.note: wasting means losing, so the abbreviation for time is lost from the word

parts.note: halt means stop
T is the abbreviation for time
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A creature beyond a stop sign, idling, is circled by light.
explanation.walkthrough: Ens is a philosophers' term, the Latin for a being; 'rings' is a verb, not a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: To enhalo is to surround with a halo, a ring of light, so enhalos means rings with light.

clue.text: Medicine is surprisingly hard on us

indicators.note: a surprising result is unexpected in form, so the letters come out in a new arrangement

parts.note: the eight letters to rearrange
bark, as in Peruvian bark, is itself a word for medicinal tree bark

explanation.surface: A patient complains that the medication is unexpectedly tough on them.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay gives only the first word; BARK comes from the definition itself, since medicinal barks are simply called bark.
explanation.definitionFit: Honduras bark is the bark of a Central American tree, cascara amarga, once used as a tonic remedy.

clue.text: So this huff could find you chewing up cheroots

indicators.note: chewing mangles something, so these letters are mashed into new order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange
taken as written: together with the answer it makes the anagram

explanation.surface: Someone in a sulk might be found chomping on cigars.
explanation.walkthrough: A compound anagram: 'So this' means SO plus the answer together rearrange CHEROOTS, so remove SO from those letters. Huff here is a verb, to bully.
explanation.definitionFit: To huff someone is an old sense meaning to bully or bluster at them, which is what hector means.

clue.text: Finding assembly go and talk freely

indicators.note: letters set free are no longer bound to their order, so they are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of 'go' and 'talk' to rearrange, 'and' joining them

explanation.surface: On finding a meeting, people go along and chat without restraint.
explanation.definitionFit: A kgotla is a traditional public meeting or tribal council in Botswana.

clue.text: Capacity of Sephardim?

indicators.note: the letters are taken out of the following word, lying inside it

parts.note: the letters inside the word, after its first

explanation.surface: How large a congregation of Sephardic Jews might be.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the measure is Hebrew, apt for the Sephardim, Jews of Spanish and Portuguese descent.
explanation.definitionFit: An epha (ephah) is an ancient Hebrew dry measure, a unit of capacity.

clue.text: Very small item or an object a long way away?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an old British coin worth a quarter of a penny, so something tiny

definitions.text: an object a long way away?
definitions.meaning: second meaning: read as two words, a thing that is distant

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the split reading FAR THING. A farthing was the smallest pre-decimal British coin.
explanation.definitionFit: A farthing, the quarter-penny coin, came to mean the least possible amount, as in 'not worth a farthing'.

clue.text: Second of three virtues daughter trusted

parts.note: faith, hope and charity are the three theological virtues; hope comes second
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A daughter relied on hope, the second of the virtues.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second' tempts you to take a second letter, but it means the second item in a list.
explanation.definitionFit: To have hoped is to have trusted or expected that something would happen.

clue.text: Ribbing husband seen in greasy spoon

indicators.note: something seen in a place is inside it, so one part goes within the other

parts.note: a caff is British slang for a cheap café, also called a greasy spoon
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A husband gets teased while eating at a cheap café.
explanation.walkthrough: H goes inside CAFF.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaff is light-hearted teasing or banter, which is what ribbing is.

clue.text: One Redcap on top of independent fighting group

indicators.note: in a down entry, being on top means coming first, so the parts are written in sequence

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
redcaps are the British military police
I is the abbreviation for independent

explanation.surface: A single military policeman stands over an independent band of fighters.
explanation.walkthrough: A redcap is a British military policeman, from their red caps.
explanation.definitionFit: An impi is a Zulu regiment, a body of warriors.

clue.text: Girl of the east, old Philippine native

parts.note: mor is an East Anglian dialect word for a girl
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: An oriental girl is an ancient inhabitant of the Philippines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The east' sounds like Asia, but it means East Anglia in England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Moros are the Muslim peoples of the southern Philippines, named from the Spanish for Moor.

clue.text: Tax bar historically — it often sounds the end

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a charge for using a road or bridge
second meaning: in old law, to bar or cancel a right or claim
third meaning: the slow ringing of a bell, as at a death

explanation.walkthrough: There are three senses here; the middle one is an old legal sense, to toll a right being to bar it.
explanation.definitionFit: A toll is a levy for passage, and a bell's toll is the slow ringing heard for a death or funeral.

clue.text: Live pro tem by river with archetypal selfie pose

parts.note: the Cam is the river through Cambridge
the pout is the classic face made in a selfie

explanation.surface: Staying temporarily by a river, someone strikes the usual selfie face.
explanation.definitionFit: To camp out is to live somewhere temporarily, for the time being, often roughly.

clue.text: Cultured pearl, pure Natal

indicators.note: cultured pearls are grown artificially, so these letters are cultivated into a new form

parts.note: the nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A flawless farmed pearl from the South African province of Natal.
explanation.walkthrough: Natal looks like the place, but it is the adjective about birth.
explanation.definitionFit: Puerperal relates to childbirth and the period just after it, as natal relates to birth.

clue.text: Old Scottish harbours on fixed terms finally

parts.note: a bone that is reset has been fixed

indicators.note: only the final letter of the word just before it is used

parts.note: the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: Scottish ports of old agreed to fixed conditions in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harbours' looks like ports, but it is a verb: in old Scots law to reset was to receive stolen goods or shelter a criminal.
explanation.definitionFit: Reset is an old Scots law term for receiving or sheltering, the same sense as harbouring a fugitive.

clue.text: Estate that is overturning confusing reflections

indicators.note: overturning flips something over, so it is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: an alod (allod) is an estate held outright, free of any feudal lord
i.e. is the abbreviation for 'that is'

explanation.surface: A property is upended, which baffles the mirror images.
explanation.walkthrough: ALOD plus IE, reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: Eidola are phantoms or insubstantial images, the kind of ghostly reflection that perplexes.
